movie_name: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings

reviews.text: At its best, The Legend Of The 10 Rings is a lot of fun – fast moving, lithe and very witty.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: We have a film that serves as an important step in terms of improved global representation, but also serves as a spectacular rollercoaster ride full of enchantment and sentimentality.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: After “Avengers: Endgame” (2019), MCU movies have been adequate, but not exhilarating whereas “Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings” leaves you wanting more because of the humor, character development, poignant, dynamic trajectory of the story
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Tony Leung is as good as advertised, but the rest of this movie struggles to live up to that performance.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Shang Chi's strongest element is how it handles relationships between family and friends.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: THIS IS A GAME CHANGER For the Asian Community, For the MCU when it comes to Debut/Origin Films, & Overall Simu’s Career! The MCU has a brand new hero
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Through the outstanding mix of long takes, impressive fighting choreography, and jaw-dropping stunt work, Simu Liu shines with his martial arts skills, but also in tackling the identity issues of the protagonist.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Thrilling and entertaining from start to finish, Shang-Chi cements itself as easily one of the best films in the MCU franchise.
reviews.author: Tyler Strandberg

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is obsessed with its backstory for the better. It's fun, it's exciting, and it's sure to rejuvenate the interest in youth practicing martial arts.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: All in all, it’s one of the best Marvel flicks of the past decade, and easily one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: I left the theater wanting to parkour onto a bus, leap into a construction site and dragon kick some bad guys in their throats. And then sing some karaoke.
reviews.author: Joseph Garcia

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings combines compelling characters, awe-inspiring action, and effective emotion to create a stunning superhero spectacle - and one of the best Marvel movies in years.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings brings Hong Kong martial arts action to the Marvel Cinematic Universe with an Asian American twist, creating a beautiful blend of East and West styles.
reviews.author: Ron Seoul-Oh

reviews.text: A few issues with the writing and the direction keep “Shang-Chi” from being top-tier MCU. But you’ll find that there is enough scattered throughout the film’s 132 minutes to keep you entertained.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: "I really really liked the film and thought it was a good origin story."
reviews.author: Kay-B

reviews.text: While it still hits every single MCU storytelling beat, Shang-Chi at least manages to evolve the franchise's action and provide a bit of refreshing diversity to the superhero world.
reviews.author: Jessie Gender

reviews.text: Just when you think they've run out of tricks, "Shang-Chi And The Legend Of The Ten Rings" will remind you once again why you love Marvel.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: SHANG-CHI AND THE LEGEND OF THE TEN RINGS is a fun and of course very welcome addition to the MCU with a fantastic first half and a slightly weaker second half, that becomes a little bit too formulaic and CGI dominant.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings has great energy, strong direction, and a fresh new set of characters. The film makes some missteps in the second half that move it a bit too far away from the strong central conflict between father and son.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: "Not for nothing, it helps that we have the eyes of Tony Leung to transport us, to put us in the mood for following this particular love story instead of inevitably jumping forward in time to more familiar MCU destinations."
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: Thirteen years and twenty-five films in, one could be forgiven for dreading yet another destiny to fulfil, another climactic battle to win. However, (this film) gives us a reason to care, and enough breadcrumbs to prove there are exciting things ahead.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: For those who are fans of basic and paint-by-numbers martial arts origin stories, Shang-Chi will be perfect but for anyone expecting anything fresh or new, keep looking
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Even if youre not a fan of the MCU and have never seen a single one of its films, Leung playing a villain in a production like this should be reason enough to at least give this rodeo show a quick run.
reviews.author: Wilson Kwong

reviews.text: After thirteen years and countless films, how does a movie studio continue to build its comic adaptation empire without feeling stale. Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is the kind of film that helps answer that question.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is one of Marvels best solo offerings yet.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Perhaps it's Cretton's occasional lack of vision or Marvel playing everything a little safe, but nonetheless, this is an exciting new start for Marvel and hopefully, the dawn of a new, more inclusive era for the studio.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: Shang-Chi brought the MCU back full-blast as director Destin Daniel Cretton seamlessly leaps from small-scale dramatic work (Short Term 12 and Just Mercy) to heartfelt martial-arts epic.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: Strong visuals, acting, and a fresh interesting story that is artfully told. Good humor, breathtaking action, and dazzling art direction. This is a strong entertaining film!
reviews.author: Ross Anthony

reviews.text: A superhero saga that, despite several exciting interludes, feels more mechanical and less spontaneous than nearly every MCU title that preceded it.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: It is a lot of fun for many different reasons.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is full of some great martial arts action and fun CG spectacle while being free of the MCU uninteresting villain curse that these origin movies often suffer from...
reviews.author: David Hogan

reviews.text: It's one of the worst I've seen in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, especially in the early phase four. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: ...as legends go, the ten rings offer a suitably epic, crowd-pleasing feel....
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: It's a worthy Marvel outing that almost gets eaten alive by monsters - but only almost.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: ...generally fares better than most similarly-themed fare...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: One of the nicest and more unexpected surprises in the recent Marvel Cinematic Universe.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: An irresistible, relentlessly fun blockbuster that balances light entertainment with dramatic weight. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Director Destin Daniel Cretton has chosen to bombard us with computer-generated images and very busy visual effects while we sort out who's who and what's at stake.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Instead of a Marvel movie, this definitely feels like a Disney film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gabriela Meza

reviews.text: Shang-Chi eloquently rewrites the character with the best of Hong Kong and Chinese cinema. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: For fans of cinematic spectacle, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings offers some of the best choreographed action sequences of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: A breath of fresh air for the superhero genre. Its high doses of adrenaline combine with visually striking action sequences and a moving story about pride and family. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is not only a winner as far as something the critics and crowds will love, but is also something that truly has meaningful and wanted representation and will be rewarded for it.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: The nods to wuxia epics like Hero and Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon are eye-catching, and the scene-stealing return of a notable MCU character delivers laughs...
reviews.author: Jeremy Aspinall

reviews.text: I didn't even need my inner 15-year-old boy to enjoy this latest Marvel blockbuster; the mature adult me was mesmerized by it.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: It's personal, obvious, and exposition for forthcoming, bigger-scale entries. A fun, exhilarating ride that entertains while sharing one more piece of the MCU's [puzzle].
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is a beautifully choreographed, heartfelt origin story that neatly wraps a fractured family's story into the Marvel superhero world.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: Shang-Chi has been introduced to the MCU by the right people and in the right ways in the very good Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: (Tony) Leung brings all the necessary depths to make his role of Wenwu far from just your garden-variety Marvel antagonist.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Action films often skimp on character development in favor fight scenes, but that is not the case here, in fact, character development is not overlooked in most Marvel action films.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is one of the better superhero flicks we've seen in recent years.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Sometimes, an MCU film, like Shang-Chi, is released that combines its louder, blockbuster values with a deeply human center, a magnificent, empathetic spark that reminds worn naysayers (admittedly like myself) what this unmatched series is capable of.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings isn't just a great addition to the MCU, it is one of its tentpoles, offering a solid foundation in which to build new stories and create new heroes that fit perfectly within the ever-expanding Marvel universe.
reviews.author: Erin Maxwell

reviews.text: A solid addition to the MCU that offers one of the franchises best villains and several of the best fight scenes. But the mandatory MCU humor and cameos hold it back from being a top tier addition to the franchise.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: A highly enjoyable addition to Marvel's mega-franchise.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: It checked all of the boxes for me. The fight choreography, the performances and the story were all great.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: This is the best MCU film this year thus far. I really enjoyed this movie, appreciated the representation and thought there were some fantastic performances by Liu, Awkwafina and Tony Leung!
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: The first half of the film is better, and I liked it much more than I was expecting.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: The character comes of age twice in two entirely different ways...and the villain is a three-dimensional villain...a role of a lifetime, right before he's launched into superstardom..,.
reviews.author: Sucharita Tyagi

reviews.text: It's sad that Shang-Chi's strongest assets are the films it's influenced by, the film career of its main antagonist, and the brief cameos. If you take those factors away, Shang-Chi is a run-of-the-mill superhero blockbuster that is entirely forgettable.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: An entertaining mix of comedy and superhero action, this is a welcome addition to the Marvel universe that, like many MCU movies, explores loss, father issues, and learning to own your power.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Although celebrated as a representational win for Asians, the issues that lurk beneath the surface of Shang-Chi leave me wondering when a necessary reckoning will happen.
reviews.author: Mimi Wong

reviews.text: A great addition to the Marvel Universe. Simu Liu and Awkwafina provide, drama, action and comedy.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: With every beat of the story feeling like an intense relapse of forced tension, the film becomes stupefyingly excessive in its last third.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: It's a forgettable comic book adaptation that promises something spectacular but left me scratching my head wondering if I had missed it. There's no magic in this Marvel tale.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It's an exciting, surprisingly sweet action fantasy, with a dazzling dynamic superhero...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings bodes well for the continued storytelling success of the MCU. It's at its best when it focuses on the innate martial arts abilities of its hero and the unique story of his family.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: For me, it's another origin story that's hopefully setting up more risk-taking surprises in movies to come.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: It's a strong debut for a new hero, injecting diverse blood into the MCU in a way that does not feel forced or hollow. I just think the overall film is still less than the sum of its more outstanding parts.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: [It] has a certain spiritual calmness to it amidst the gorgeously choreographed action sequences. Never has a Marvel movie felt this unique in its execution and treatment. If you are looking for a film to end your big screen abstinence, this is the one.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: A run of decent fights early on and some fun chemistry between the two leads provides some strong bedrock for what turns out to be a fairly solid, if only moderately spectacular, Marvel origin story
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: From where this critic is sitting, Cretton and his creative team have delivered the most purely enjoyable MCU release since Ant-Man and the Wasp back in 2018...
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: While it still falls into some of the trappings of Marvel's less compelling aspects, it still manages to be a big entertaining time at the movies and an interesting expansion on the larger cinematic universe it's set in.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Despite the sketchy scripting, the vehicular chase through San Francisco is the best since 'Bullitt' (1968).
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: While largely entertaining - the film's big serving of action is balanced by a good bit of comedy - Shang-Chi isn't quite on the level of Black Panther.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings kicks ass...thrilling and funny and surprisingly poignant, a wonderful mélange of on-point action, drama and humor with a just-right amount of fan service and overarching story connection.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: In the end, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings comes across as more cookie-cutter and generic because I have seen better Asian films. It's a competent film, but don't expect anything more than a Marvel blockbuster.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Flits between offering up a lively picture that strives to carve out its own space in the series, and simply serving up more of the usual Marvel template but in enticing packaging.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: ... this is a terrific, entry-level work that delivers on far more visceral action than we're used to from these films.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The work of director Destin Daniel Cretton and the entire creative team behind the film deserves a standing ovation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: This superhero origin story features some creatively choreographed, over-the-top martial arts mayhem while sacrificing much of its character depth and relevant cultural context along the way.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Overly busy on numerous levels, but proves it's better to have too many elements than not enough.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings at least continues the studio's track record of enlisting the talents of truly great artists. Here, that would be the commanding and charismatic Leung.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Shang-Chi works because it plays more like a classical martial arts movie than a typical Marvel film.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Great action, Simu Liu is a great kind of charismatic center for [the film].
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: What makes this film such a joy are the embellishments added on to the well-worn narrative.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Aided by a formidable performance from Hong Kong superstar Tony Leung, director Destin Daniel Cretton doesn't quite remake the Marvel wheel so much as he enlivens it with the kinetic, charming and surprisingly heartfelt Shang-Chi.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Director Destin Daniel Cretton breaks with traditional Marvel storytelling and uses flashbacks to propel the narrative forward. The approach emotionally charges an otherwise standard superhero origin story.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: One of the most exhilarating Marvel movies yet.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Deserves its rightful place as one of the best MCU films to date.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Shang-Chi doesn't reinvent the wheel but shows us the peak of the MCU.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: In a summer with films that used the family dynamic to create dramatic tension, Shang-Chi does it as good as any -- with some strong emotional moments.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Shang-Chi pilfers from already familiar and much more original and artistic Chinese martial-arts genre movies -- reducing them to the level of Marvel junk.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The picture rattles along with an unpretentious vigour too rare in the Marvel universe.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: If Shang-Chi isn't as all-encompassing an achievement as Black Panther, it is up to the standard of quality set by the other Marvel films, and its ties to Asian folklore and traditions of filmmaking set it apart from the rest of that canon.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: It feeds the fantasies of leaving your day job for some glorious adventure while acknowledging families are not always so picture perfect.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: It's a good movie. It's got a plausibly fearsome villain by way of Leung, a nice ensemble of heroic personalities, and a dose of actually-poignant family drama undergirding all the rest.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Thanks to the exciting talent in front of and behind the camera, the film undoubtedly deserves a look, but it's far from the great success it could have been. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Not since Black Panther has the world of a Marvel film felt so vibrantly alive.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The picture would be worth seeing just to watch Tony Leung command the screen every minute he's on it.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Shang-Chi's character arc from car valet to superhero is a joy to watch, and Liu plays it with the right amount of charm and seriousness.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: The thrilling stunts and elaborate martial arts and fight choreography create action sequences as elegant as they are exciting.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Top tier MCU movie with dazzling action sequences + fight choreography, but the emotional father-son dynamic humanizes the fantastical narrative. Tony Leung brings immense gravitas to the role + Simu Liu emerges as a formidable action hero.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: It introduces us to a whole other world, steeped in mythology and authenticity, and it's a superhero origin story unlike any other. Dragon-sized epic and deeply personal, 'Shang-Chi' is a sheer spectacle and heartfelt joy to watch.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Its cultural impact is enormous, as it arrives when hate crimes against Asians in America is on the rise.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The likable persona of Simi Liu & comic relief of Awkwafina are highlights, despite the turn into an ancient Chinese village (wouldn't the govt. had built a factory on it?).
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is the best of the Marvel origin stories yet.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Shang-Chi reimagines the superhero blockbuster through the lens of a new, more diverse, generation and what immerges is a story better in every respect.
reviews.author: Alicia Gilstorf

reviews.text: When given a chance to define its own lane, Shang-Chi integrates some much-needed vitality to the familiar proceedings.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: In a movie serving as backstory, an origin story, and even another MCU expansion, the reinvent button on the impeding "superhero fatigue" machine is mashed yet again with a satisfying character-driven adventure... and one of the best Marvel films to date.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Shang-Chi grabbed me like Tony Stark did way back in Phase One, and he did it without being a Tony Stark clone.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: You can almost see Marvel Studios reaching out to a wider world, desperately trying to entertain while being culturally respectful and causing as little offence as possible. A tough balancing act, but one it pulls off with an impressively light touch.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Liu... brings flair, grace and a touch of steel to an ageing Avengers line-up.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: A metatextual antithesis to the racism and whitewashing in Marvel's own history, and a cinematic celebration of the Chinese diaspora on and off screen.
reviews.author: Weiting Liu

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings toes the line carefully, delivering exactly the energy we expect from a Marvel film and more, even if it leans too much into the humor at the expense of real depth.
reviews.author: Jon Espino

reviews.text: When Tony Leung is onscreen, he's the only thing it's possible to care about, and when he's not onscreen, it's hard not to wonder what he's up to.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Shang-Chi, from its flat composition and mechanical editing, to its low-key score, is a curiously muted offering.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: The great news: Superheroland has its first Asian lead . . . Even better, he's portrayed by aw-shucks newcomer Simu Liu, who simply explodes onto the screen early during a boffo bus-fight segment.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It's vanishingly rare for a film to actually deserve its hype. But Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings does so, and more.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Shang Chi And The Legend Of The Ten Rings is a strong step forward for the MCU.
reviews.author: Anupama Chopra

reviews.text: When the conflicts are this personal, one is bound to get invested.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: Simu Liu is a superstar in the making, ably taking on the title role with the confidence of a veteran of ten blockbusters, and holds his own against a cinema legend like Tony Leung.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Shang-Chi: The Legend of the Ten Rings marks the first time a Marvel movie has felt machine-manufactured to the point of being laborious.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: It's a standard story, and it absolutely works... It's unique to the Marvel Universe because it's the first time they've done this.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: I found it incredibly wonderful how they splice all these genres together. It's faithful to Marvel, but it's also very faithful to the traditions it's importing.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is one of the best films in the MCU, featuring the most incredible fight scenes I have seen on film and a refreshing script exuding tremendous heart.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: The special effects and flying dragons are all elegant and occasionally impressive but become tedious long before the film bangs and wheezes to its get-ready-for-the-sequel conclusion...
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is one of the best MCU films since Black Panther.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Shang-Chi feels like a welcome step forward for Marvel, in a direction not only of inclusivity, but true creativity that we can only hope suggests further interesting developments to come.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Cretton has fashioned a credible mash-up of Chinese mythology and superhero orthodoxy, producing something that feels of a piece with the basic MCU tenets and singular in its cultural detail.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: An all-around excellent origin story, which features among the most exhilarating action in the Marvel series, continues the franchise's trend of showcasing much better villains than it used to, and builds to a surprisingly ambitious second half.
reviews.author: Brendan Morrow

reviews.text: Almost any movie ascending out of the Marvel Cinematic Universe at this point requires a classicist's devotion to subtextual minutiae. Which is exactly why Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is such a breath of freshly fantastical air.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings does develop connections to the larger Marvel universe. But the best compliment to the movie is the fact that it doesn't need them.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: [The] film is peppered with marvellous fight sequences and only gets a trifle overblown towards the end. Its secret weapon is Awkwafina, whose effortless comic timing constantly undercuts potential outbreaks of pomposity.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Director Destin Cretton and cinematographer Bill Pope have created such a rich visual language for this film that it is unlike anything we've previously experienced in the MCU.
reviews.author: Jamal Grootboom

reviews.text: Liu and Awkwafina have a delicate, delicious chemistry that raises this picture above the pack.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Not knowing what to expect and coming out delighted was probably my favorite part. A comfortable roller coaster of feels and fights that didn't pander to cheap lows or unrealistic highs.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Liu, also a stuntman and athlete is nimble and fearless, gracefully, effortlessly lifting the fight choreography.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: If you're a Marvel fan, enjoy action adventure/martial arts, appreciate production design...and costumes that more than please the eye, or want to be entertained, this marvelous spectacle, Shang Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings will enthrall.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: With "Shang-Chi," we get the safe and the familiar--amusing sameness floating in a sea of bland blockbuster commercially created contrivances.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The film boasts first-rate fight and chase scenes and a terrific cast. It's better than a lot of Marvel superhero films by a longshot.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: In many ways that matter, this is a step forward for superhero movies and representation. In many others, it stays regrettably rooted to the spot.
reviews.author: James Hanton

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is an upper-echelon MCU film, and like the very best of them, it only leaves you salivating for the next installment.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Simu Liu steps into his role effortlessly. The pieces are more impressive than the whole.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is the most dynamic, fun, clever MCU solo film since Black Panther.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: Shang-Chi delivers an intimate origin story wrapped around an action packed adventure with some of the best action the MCU has ever seen.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Does it work? Of course. Marvel hasn't truly missed in a long time.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: So what if the showoff climax subs depth for dazzle. As the first Asian hero in Marvel history, former stuntman Simu Liu is action poetry in motion and his epic starring debut kicks off the fall film season on a rousing high note.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings isn't top-tier MCU, but it's a solid origin story anchored by two fantastic performances from Simu Liu and Tony Leung, as well as some of the franchise's best action.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: As an origin story, "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings" works very well, and as an action-fantasy movie, it isn't too bad either. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is nothing short of action movie perfection; this is the MCU like you've never seen before, and it's no exaggeration to say Simu Liu was born to play the MCU's newest Avenger.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: Packed with a ton to like but little to love (or hate), audiences will leave Chi with frosting on their lips while cinema aficionados once more bemoan nothing substantial on their hips.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings" exemplifies Marvel Studios' credibility and is supplied with plenty of heart and soul.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Geeky subtext aside, the film manages to connect with non-MCU obsessives by offering thrills, chills and laughs.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: More so than his fists and fights...Shang-Chi is defined by the struggles of the heart, and that's often a much more interesting battle than any supervillain scheme.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is effective because the stakes remain relatively small. It is, essentially, a family melodrama.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and Katy are my new best friends.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A thrilling, fun and exhilarating slice of mindless entertainment.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Long live Tony Leung and Michelle Yeoh, who make a movie better by just walking into it.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: It's a Marvel film for a Gen-Z crowd, ashamed of the more archaic avenues that the franchise has previously walked down, but also willing to engage with and ultimately embrace woke-minded alternatives.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: "Shang-Chi" is a diverting popcorn movie that should provide Marvel fans with the action fix they yearn for.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Time will tell how well Shang-Chi penetrates into the mainstream, but it succeeds in throwing even a little bit of a curveball compared to the standard Marvel fare.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: This latest Marvel movie has enough positive elements (action, humor and a story with deep family roots) to constitute an entertaining addition to Marvel's apparently endless stream of movies.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Shang-Chi isn't a must-see, but it's an engaging action movie brimming with both style and soul.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Somehow, still, director Destin Daniel Cretton (Just Mercy, Short Term 12) finds space to let blossom a genuinely touching emotive backstory for our immortal archvillain and a (however fleeting) fresh perspective on a martial arts master.
reviews.author: Jay Horton

reviews.text: A celebration of flying-fist flicks with a history-making lead? This one feels like something new -- not just for Marvel, but for American blockbuster cinema.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: Each half is solid enough that Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings really could have been two separate films: An origin story and its bombastic sequel.
reviews.author: Skylar Ezell

reviews.text: If the thrilling Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings portends what is to come for the Marvel Cinematic Universe in its next phase, by all means, sign me up.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: I won't be unhappy to see Shang-Chi again when he pops up in some inevitable side-quel, but I wish he weren't beholden to shared-universe machinations, instead of being the master of his magical domain.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Shang-Chi takes Marvel's action choreography to a new level of thrilling and the camera dances with the movement.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: [Wenwu] wasn't just a one-dimensiona bad guy and I think Marvel does a really great job with this.
reviews.author: Achara Kirk

reviews.text: [The action scenes were] amazing, not just the way it was choreographed but the way it was shot it.
reviews.author: Jaby Koay

reviews.text: Star Simu Liu effortlessly inhabits the role of Shang-Chi, deftly balancing the contemplative, introspective side of the character without coming off as overly dour.
reviews.author: Sam Stone

reviews.text: Shang-Chi doesn't just pull off a fun western xuanhuan, but makes it feel like a door being opened for future Marvel films.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: 'Shang-Chi' isn't some sort of genre masterpiece. It's not even in the upper tier of Marvel movies. But it is good, old-fashioned dorky B-movie fun.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: One of the fresher, more engaging installments in the mostly exhausting onslaught of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Are we facing a new movie star? Most likely. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Simu Liu is perfect as Shang-Chi. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: Simu Liu and his character Shang-Chi will have a lasting impact on the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Liu brings a natural presence to the film. He's charming, soulful, and makes for a great pair with Awkwafina.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: A funny, pulpy martial arts movie that draws from the big wuxia crossover successes of the early 2000s... and fuses them with the quippy, nerdy, endearingly goofy character work Marvel does really well.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Cretton's brisk pacing as well as much self-referential humor insures we don't take things too seriously.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Yes, "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings" is culturally significant, but this should not be lost: It's also a fantastic movie.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: It's fresh, it's alive, it's not the same old Marvel Cinematic Universe. There are also awesome dragons.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: "Shang-Chi" holds his own, but he doesn't leave you wanting more. It feels like a one-and-done while we get back to the main attraction.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: [W]hen it finally comes time for the screenwriters to come up with [a plot], they seem uncertain about what to do...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: As the MCU emerges from the long shadow of the Infinity Saga, the newest members of the ever-growing ensemble make a compelling case for belonging among the candidates for the next iteration of The Avengers.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: [A] refreshing romp through - and loving homage to - martial arts cinema.
reviews.author: Cliff Lee

reviews.text: There's much to like in this offering, especially when it's pulling inspiration from and feeding off the vibe of Jackie Chan in his prime.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings succeeds because of its action, its cast and story but most of all it works because of its sincerity.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A movie that works both as a stand-alone action adventure and a fresh, fast-paced addition to the comic book Marvel universe
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: There are plenty of appealing new elements in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, but it's still an MCU movie, for better and worse.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Fortunately, the picture knows how to make fun of itself, smartly casting Awkwafina as a comically down-to-earth sidekick.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Paging Scorsese, if the MCU is good enough for Tony Leung Chiu-wai, it should be good enough for all the cinephile snobs out there.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: They say a hero is only as good as his villain, but casting Tony Leung as the main antagonist keeps Shang-Chi walking in his shadow throughout the entire movie. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: Liu shines as the protagonist, and Awkwafina offers excellent support, the rapport between them lending the film its funniest moments.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: As Wenwu, Tony Leung Chiu Wai is sensitively framed by director Cretton in a way that emphasises the Hong Kong veteran's most evocative weapon: his eyes.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Marvel appear to have more than found a worthy player to sit high upon the action mantle with his more well-known counterparts.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, the film is somewhat overstuffed and lumpy in parts and the last surreal third is poorly knitted into the rest of the narrative, but it's all impossible to predict and you'll leave the theater satisfied.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: Shang-Chi isn't a hopeless addition to the Marvel Cinematic Universe fold. But the movie feels as racked with a sense of inadequacy about its main character as that main character is about himself...
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: A full-blooded Marvel film, colorful, exhilarating, funny, and full of hope.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Shang-Chi takes me back to the wuxia & other martial arts films I grew up with but also blends pop culture with Chinese mythology. It's a bit hodge-podge in parts but the cast is fab and the story ties in nicely to the larger MCU. Also Tony Leung forever.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: You can appreciate and enjoy what the film tries to do, and what it accomplishes, while still wishing for something more.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: I fear for the sequel, as I do for all Marvel sequels, because so often they're about delivering another round of the expected. But "Shang-Chi" may succeed there, too. It certainly succeeds here.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The film uses the superficial markers of Asian culture and filmmaking without presenting anything unique in its Marvel take on that tradition.
reviews.author: Maya Phillips

reviews.text: A minor film, but very endearing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: Disney-Marvel's first Asian lead superhero makes a semi-impressive debut.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Drawing on other genres and incorporating more points of view in the creative process is all the familiar formula needs to feel fresh...
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Razzle dazzle - with a ton of heart and a generous sprinkling of warm humor. That's "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings" right there.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The film rests on the performance of Liu who makes the leap from the small screen (Kim's Convenience). Charismatic in the quietest way, his Shang-Chi has a moral core, and doesn't need to dominate.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Will definitely get your blood pumping! It's got representation, amazing world-building and the MCU's best hand-to-hand, martial arts choreography. One of the best "origin" entries of the MCU. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Shang-Chi was a spectacle. It was fresh, and fun, and engaging throughout. It was exactly what you would expect from Marvel, and it was refreshing to see a new addition to the ever-growing roster of Marvel heroes on the silver screen.
reviews.author: Ciaran Kerr

reviews.text: The by-the-numbers second half fortunately doesn't dim the sparkle of the film's first half, or the obvious rightness of Simu Liu in the role of Shang-Chi.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The film's fulsome embrace of martial arts adds impact and polish to the action, giving it a scaled-down sense of spectacle that's often very satisfying.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: An exciting, heartfelt origin story with a wow of a fight scene on an articulated bus.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The look and feel of the film is mesmerizing, but perhaps what's even more captivating are the performances by this outstanding cast.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: "..doesn't feel like just another MCU installment, which is a compliment. The characters are fresh and Cretton constantly emphasizes the emotional connections between them, crafting a modern, wuxia-informed martial arts movie with heart.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Loved it from start to finish; action, humor, and fantasy, going all out. A comic-based movie with all the comic magic which that implies [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: The script is loaded with hilarious repartee and the martial arts fight scenes are choreographed like a breathtaking ballet.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: I never thought I would write that a Marvel movie was the best of the year...but here we are.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Liu is a very welcome addition to Marvel's superhero roster. With spectacular fight choreography and gorgeous costuming, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is an entertaining, albeit narratively familiar, entry in the MCU.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a visually impressive, mythologically rich and heartfelt origin story that boasts laughs, grief and romance along with a great double-act from Simu Liu and Awkwafina.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: He used to be a minor comic character: a half-forgotten, stereotypical martial artist who first appeared in 1973 to cash in on Bruce Lee mania and the Kung Fu television series. But now Shang-Chi is a big deal.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings" certainly isn't the typical MCU entry. That's part of its appeal.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Marvel's first Asian superhero led action-fest has exceptional storytelling, nuanced characters, spectacular choreography and special effects.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: One of the best action films I've seen in a long time. Absolutely loved the introduction of Shang-Chi into the universe. The perfect dynamic between Liu & Awkwafina carry this movie & the world-building is superb & fascinating.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Marvel freshens up its formula with the fantasy-fueled origin story Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: With a stellar cast, impressively choreographed martial arts sequences and a fantastic lead performance from Simu Liu, this is a refreshing and exciting entry to the MCU.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: i thought the whole movie was entertaining to watch, but that first half -- something about its style, its pacing, the dialogue -- it just seemed has some creativity to it and had a lot of energy to it, a lot of charm to it.
reviews.author: Andre Meadows

reviews.text: It's a supremely entertaining movie on every level, and the fact that it will likely kick in the door for more Asian superheroes to take center stage in the future (Jubilee, please) is icing on the cake.
reviews.author: Bernard Boo

reviews.text: Boasts fantastic martial arts and action sequences, an all-time villain performance, and represents the integration of the MCU with an indie filmmaker that's a strong fit.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: It's perfectly fine entertainment in the moment, but the overall staying power is pretty negligible.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: Awkwafina's real super power is the ability to steal every scene, and elevate what is already an upper echelon Marvel movie into the stratosphere.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: An overreliance on CGI tempers the excitement of the action scenes until it gives into the effects entirely during a devolving stretch of underwritten characters and a story that does not do justice to its protagonist.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings made me forget I was watching a Marvel movie, and that's a good thing.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings does stick to the established formula to a degree, but it's imbued with enough passion to overcome a slightly by-the-numbers origin story blueprint and emerge as one of the MCU's strongest chapters.
reviews.author: Mark Cassidy

reviews.text: By delivering a superhero film that offers stunning performances from Liu and Leung while celebrating Asian culture ... Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a tour de force.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: A highly enjoyable tale of father-son rivalry and how to set about achieving your potential.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is a film that isn't completely sure what it wants to be, other than an Asian American hero in the MCU. The Master of Kung Fu deserves better.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is at its best when it's not trying to fit so nicely within the MCU and when it's content to be a more modest, engaging origin story.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Regardless of its flaws, I still enjoyed the movie
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: The film's main problem is its tone: it vacillates between wanting to be a Chinese blockbuster and what is expected of a Marvel superhero movie.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: It's a fun and refreshing change of pace for the MCU, but Shang-Chi falls short of being something great.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: Beneath the dazzling rings and furious fight choreography is a story about a son struggling with who he was meant to be, and fighting to leave his father's shadow.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: Starting strongly with a series of excellent action sequences and some delightful comedic banter, the franchise's 25th installment is an uneven but entertaining mixture of fresh and familiar.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: It's a stark juxtaposition, the long periods of exposition, then the story jumps back to life with beautiful set pieces and intense action... When the characters are just being the characters, instead of listening to exposition, this is a really fun movie
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Falls in the medium-low end of the MCU spectrum. Lots of flashy CGI-assisted martial arts action, but it never helps when your main character is the least interesting person onscreen.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: By turns poignant and entertaining, frantic and considered, 'Shang-Chi and The Legend of the Ten Rings' is another enjoyable addition to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings expands the Marvel lineup of characters and does it with thrilling style.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Simu Liu is Shang-Chi, master of kung-fu, and Marvel has its first Asian leading man. About damn time.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Runs maybe a bit overlong - those flashbacks! - but it's rarely less than an entertaining and at times affecting entry in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: "Shang-Chi" takes the Marvel Cinematic Universe in an exciting new direction without leaving behind all the fun and thrills. The future is in good hands.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: While the fights were entertaining to watch, none of them would've have been successful without the amazing performances from the cast.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Though Shang-Chi introduces what could've been one of Marvel's most compelling villains ever, even the magic of Tony Leung can't save the film from tumbling into mediocrity thanks to an uninspired script and a bumbling third act.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Watching Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings should yield a deeper appreciation of Chinese culture, Asian history, and the evolution of the action film.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: Effectively balancing the serious with the comic, 'Shang-Chi' is an entirely satisfying spectacle within its genre, and a very good, emotionally satisfying--and fun-super hero movie.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Shang-Chi has all the right ingredients to become the next winning franchise in the MCU.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: Liu is captivating. The Chinese-Canadian star owns every moment he is on screen - which, thankfully, is a lot.
reviews.author: Callum Crumlish

reviews.text: Much better than I anticipated, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings gives us the flavor of the MCU while changing up the dish some with new and exotic spices.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: It's always fascinating watching Marvel tackle another genre. Marvel fully kicks the door in on the martial arts arena with another explosive audience pleasing effort.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: It introduces ... Shang-Chi with plenty of the tricks the MCU used to create its box office supremacy while finally pushing the series in a mildly different direction.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings has plenty of heart and adventurous spirit to satisfy superhero movie fans. It's too bad that the title character has a personality that's duller than the average Marvel superhero.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: SHANG-CHI is a very different sort of MCU film and a welcome one to kick off the next phase in the MCU. Director Destin Daniel Cretton balances the action with humor and heart around a family drama that draws you in right away.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Characters worth knowing, adventure worth seeking, and a delightful shift in tone that will bring a distinctive new flavor to the next phase of the ongoing "Avengers" saga.
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: A killer turn from legend Tony Leung, some impressive action and sporadically moving moments can't help the fact that Simu Liu is one of the most boring MCU leads in the megafranchise's existence.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: [Shang-Chi] fits into Marvel packaging in its own way, but it has an immense soulfulness that other MCU movies, superhero movies, and action movies in general should take notes from.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: See it opening night! Packed with action and amazing imagery. You're in for a great time. The dynamic between Simu Liu and Awkwafina worked extremely well. Enjoyed that they featured various Chinese mythology and creatures as well.
reviews.author: Wendy Lee Szany

reviews.text: [L]umbers along with a weighted-down plot obsessed with backstory.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Between its fight scenes and family drama, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a welcome addition to the MCU and gives one of Marvel's most promising characters his due.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: A stylish MCU flick with amazing direction that is fun and exciting. See, Hollywood? This is what happens when you finally let an Asian director helm an Asian-led action flick
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Simu Liu, demonstrates he can carry the movie without a CGI galore climax. Shifting that route, Marvel once again proves to be their own worst enemy regarding the difference between disposable entertainment and crafting something legitimately great
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: A wondrous blend of martial arts classics with the Marvel brand, and it will always be jaw-dropping to behold on that level, regardless of the things that went wrong.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a stunning martial arts epic that absolutely shattered my already high expectations.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Getting to see [my culture] reflected in a Marvel blockbuster flick, despite its flaws, makes me excited for what more we might see from Shang-Chi.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: Shang-Chi ultimately belongs to Leung. He's not just the star of the film's opening -- in his hands, Wenwu's devastation catalyzes the action and permeates every frame, turning the film into a tragedy.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: Despite its representational bona-fides, could not be a more purely generic exercise from this machine that eats cinema.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: While we can't help wondering how much better this movie could have been untethered from the MCU at large, its distinct and fresh story make for an enjoyable watch.
reviews.author: Gabriella Geisinger

reviews.text: This is director Destin Daniel Cretton's first action film, and you would not believe it with how confidently he shoots this movie.
reviews.author: Alex Cranz

reviews.text: [Despite some last act stumbles,] there is more might to your dragon in seeing Shang-Chi as a blockbuster full of grace and values.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: It is a fantastic origin story that is very friendly for viewers like me with little to no existing Marvel knowledge. Overall, I found this movie to be a must-watch; better yet, I came out of this movie wanting to watch it again and again!
reviews.author: Josephine L.

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is refreshing in how little it's concerned with big-picture universe-building details. Instead, the movie focuses on an extremely personal story that also implies exciting things about the future of Marvel movies.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: At some point during one of the best car chase scenes in San Francisco movie history, "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings" makes at least one thing gloriously clear: Today, you will be getting your money's worth at the movies.
reviews.author: Peter Hartlaub

reviews.text: The best MCU superhero origin story since Iron Man. Enough ties to the greater franchise, while still allowing Shang-Chi to shine! Seriously epic large scale fight scenes too!
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: It's Marvel doing what Marvel does, but getting almost everything right this time - and that's rare.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: It's sad to see what could've been a rousing standalone finish its journey as little more than a pitstop to something much better.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Even though it doesn't stick the landing, Shang-Chi is one of the better Marvel intros. Thor and Captain America both debuted in films less assured than this, and look how they developed.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: A vast, multifaceted maze of complex relationships, pitch-perfect martial arts, mesmerising storytelling and explosive visuals. This is one mystical Marvel masterpiece you will want to see time and again.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: For his first blockbuster, Destin Daniel Cretton has made a genuinely fun crowd-pleaser that expands the MCU both in its setting and in its representation.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: It's a refreshing lift for this next phase of Marvel's world domination. You leave genuinely wanting to see more of Shang-Chi, even as we know we'll be meeting him again very soon.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: Enjoyable, even when the story fails to engage.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: With Shang-Chi, we have on our hands perhaps the least essential MCU affair since Mickey Rourke was throwing laser whips around Robert Downey Jr's head.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: Even with its muddy, CGI soup third act, there's a voice within Shang-Chi's kinetic action, and a powerful performance from screen legend Tony Leung as one of the MCU's best villains.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and The Legend of The Ten Rings skillfully introduces a new corner of the Marvel universe with minimal stumbles along the way.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: 'Shang-Chi' blends MCU tropes and director Destin Daniel Cretton's sensibilities into a thrilling action-fantasy that turns the "Hollywood movie aimed at Asians" formula on its head.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: a significantly higher percentage of great big floofy magic animals than I was expecting - one of which has wings, six legs and no face but kind of... 'two butts?' Anyway it's name is 'MORRIS' and your kids are gonna want one.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: Simu Liu's Shang-Chi is already a welcome addition to an already-thriving pantheon of superheroes.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Even the film's fight sequences bristle with emotion - as acts of flirtation, rage, or even love.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Top Tier Marvel. One of their best solo films. Lots of great homages to Asian cinema & culture. Leung, Awkwafina & Kingsley are standouts. Cretton knocked it out of the park!
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: The first half of the movie is funnier and more down-to-earth than its second, which transitions from modern action to mythical fantasy with an emphasis on Chinese folklore-some actual, some imagined.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: 'Shang Chi' starts out strong with some majestic martial artistry which does fade later on, but it's always visually engaging as Cretton builds an extension of the MCU that feels successfully standalone.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Despite pacing issues, it delivers a hugely entertaining step in the right direction for Asian representation.
reviews.author: Laura Sirikul

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is an artful and entertaining introduction to an exciting new hero.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: It's a Marvel movie that doesn't feel like a Marvel movie, with a fresh, snappy tone that has a lot in common with 2015's Ant-Man, which also felt like a departure from the franchise formula at the time.
reviews.author: Alexis Nedd

reviews.text: Shang-Chi certainly deserves credit as a groundbreaking step of representation in mega-budget filmmaking. You just desperately wish that the terrain it treads upon didn't feel so safe.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: It remembers to have fun. It's a kick to watch - often literally - and the kind of popcorn movie summer is made for.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It's an uneven picture, but when "Legend of the Ten Rings" concentrates on raw power and unusual obstacles, it's the type of electrifying superhero introduction that every fringe character should enjoy.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Marvel's Phase Four makes up for lost time with an origin story that richly entertains when it's not pushing boundaries.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is one of the Marvel Cinematic Universe's best origin stories to date, filled with stunningly choreographed action, unexpected laughs, and a whole lot of heart.
reviews.author: Jamie Jirak

reviews.text: A Technicolor whirlwind of a film whose explosive fight choreography and dense mythology are leavened by a sweet and surprisingly nimble script.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: A solid coming of age tale about accepting your past while forging your own path forward that features some downright stellar set pieces -- true MCU standouts.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: [T]he action on display is brilliant and unlike anything we've ever seen before in a Marvel Studios release.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Ventures in a new direction, building on the world that has become common moviegoer knowledge, but adding stylistic flourishes and an unhurried pace from Cretton that suggests it's content to be its own story instead of a cog in a larger machine.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Quibbles aside, "Shang-Chi" is another smartly calibrated extension of the Marvel stable amid its endeavors to become more diverse.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings presents a bright future for Marvel Studios and the expanded cinematic universe.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Marvel's first foray into the fantasy genre, drawing from traditional Chinese legends to create a visually-and tonally-distinct departure from previous origin endeavors.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Liu... is simply a joy to watch. He's the MCU's most significant and infectious rookie since the late Chadwick Boseman with the same face-of-the-franchise appeal as Chris Evans.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: The best standalone MCU film since Black Panther.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: While its disparate elements don't meld together as smoothly as they should, they do, in the end, add up to a superhero movie fresh and fun enough to feel worth a spin.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: A hero's origin story that tries, with some success, to rise above Marvel business-as-usual.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: A world of Asian mysticism, with dragons, demons, and creatures-think Asian Wuxia movies like "House of Flying Daggers" meets "Raya The Last Dragon"-that feels unique to what we've already seen in the mystic side of the MCU.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: Shang-Chi—as the first Asian American superhero to headline a film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe—is a necessary and worthy addition to the pantheon and Hollywood as a whole.
reviews.author: Nancy Wang Yuen

reviews.text: The strongest MCU origin story to date, Simu Liu commands as Shang-Chi, bringing layered nuance to the role. Action sequences are tightly executed and draw the eye.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is about family told with a lot of humor and a lot of Asian faces to fill out the diversity in the MCU.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: Awkwafina and Simu Liu make for the perfect acting duo; they have great friendship chemistry and comedic timing. They share the infamous fight sequence aboard a moving Muni bus in San Francisco. She does the hilly driving, he does the kicking of ass.
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: One of Marvel's messiest efforts, with a stellar front half that quickly retreats back to the studio's comfort zone.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: On the screen, Shang-Chi is rotely defined by the same "gifted kid" impostor syndrome as so many other self-doubting MCU heroes before him.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: As the MCU only continues to expand, Cretton's film should be pointed to as a sterling example of what's possible when a hero is allowed to be his own man, on his own terms.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: This thoroughly engaging reimagination of the Marvel comic book that debuted in the '70s has been retrofitted for its movie debut, and the results are encouraging to say the least.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings showcases a type of action often undervalued in the MCU while offering a fresh origin of a hero we're yet to see on screen.
reviews.author: Amelia Emberwing

reviews.text: It's an entertaining romp, although the formulaic quality is becoming a little obvious.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is as bland and busy as its title.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a confident introduction to Marvel's first Asian superhero, delivering the MCU's best fight choreography and one of its most emotionally complex villains.
reviews.author: Francesca Rivera

reviews.text: A mostly decent Marvel movie buoyed by crisp, kinetic action and the Marvel Cinematic Universe's best "villain" yet.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: A flashy, Asian-led visual effects extravaganza that gives the second-tier hero the same over-the-top treatment that big-timers like Hulk and Thor typically get.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Bolstered by a star-making performance from Simu Liu, ﻿Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings gets the MCU's newest hero off to a promising start.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: Marvel has its best solo film in years with this action-filled magical adventure.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: It's a solidly constructed superhero origin story, steeped in a beautifully rendered view of the hero's cultural ties, with some strong performers, and a connection back to the whole Marvel Cinematic Universe.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: ...dares to question the potency of the MCU punchplosion.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is a total knockout. The balance of humor and heart is surprisingly solid, but the action is next level. It features some of the best choreography I have seen in a long time.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings has equal amounts of action, heart, and humor. The result is as satisfying an outing as Marvel has had in some time.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: A pulse-pounding great time at the movies
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Shang-Chi is sure to make its mark as an important milestone of representation in the history of superhero cinema.
reviews.author: Diego Andaluz

reviews.text: ... director Destin Daniel Cretton's Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings feels more like a modern wuxia tale than the standard American actioner, using the action to communicate the internal in ways subtle and blatant and absolutely engaging.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a genuine triumph for Marvel Studios, a true family drama with plenty of charm and a myriad of winning performances!
reviews.author: Rohan Patel

reviews.text: [Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings] has the best fights ever in an MCU film and is one of my favorite Hollywood martial arts films.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: Marvel is back and Simu Liu is a star!
reviews.author: Brian Frederick

synopsis: Marvel Studios' "Shang-Chi and The Legend of The Ten Rings" stars Simu Liu as Shang-Chi, who must confront the past he thought he left behind when he is drawn into the web of the mysterious Ten Rings organization. The film also stars Tony Leung as Wenwu, Awkwafina as Shang-Chi's friend Katy and Michelle Yeoh as Jiang Nan, as well as Fala Chen, Meng'er Zhang, Florian Munteanu and Ronny Chieng.
